newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee steady vs dollar in forward, spot.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee steady vs dollar in forward, spot.

text.p: The Indian rupee was steady against both the forward and spot dollar in quiet late-morning trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
January-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 0.67/0.69 rupee against Monday's close of 0.66/0.68, dealers said.
"Initially we had expected forward premiums to go up on tighter liquidity after yesterday's bond auction," said a dealer at a foreign bank.

The central bank raised 50 billion rupees through an auction of four-year federal government bonds on Monday. Outflows towards the bond pushed up call money rates to 7.50-8.25 in late-morning Tuesday against Monday's closing of 3.25-3.50.
"But market players expect interest rates to stay down and this is keeping premiums from going up," he said.
In the spot market, the rupee was stuck in a narrow band between 35.6975 and 35.7000 per dollar in light trade, dealers said.
They said dollar demand was poor and the Reserve Bank of India had not yet bought dollars on Tuesday.
